tie_order_reconciliation.explanation: The two extra cases swap equal-score anchors while membership and packet receipts stay identical. NumPy default argsort is not stable for ties; changing other documents zero-vote scores can change the order of tied positive-vote anchors. The one unchanged case retains a zero-score lexical anchor after its RRF credit is removed.

source_impact_review.question: How many days ago did I buy a smoker?
source_impact_review.observation: The swapped original turns discuss assistant personality or interview/artist topics, not smoker purchase timing. Neither arm gains or loses annotated smoker evidence. Saved answer remains not mentioned; no new answer was run.

source_impact_review.question: Who became a parent first, Tom or Alex?
source_impact_review.observation: Positive-only lexical voting removes an unrelated hello exchange. Baseline and both arms contain Alex-parent evidence but no Tom-parent timestamp; annotated presence is unchanged. Saved historical answer Alex was incorrect, and no new answer was run.

limits: Changed anchor ordering can result from unstable NumPy tie sorting even when no selected zero-keyword anchor appears in the prior diagnosis; equal-score swaps had no packet effect here.
Zero TF-IDF cosine does not mean semantic irrelevance; dense votes and source eligibility remained.
Annotated text presence and source receipts do not measure final-answer correctness, and the frozen baseline itself was not temporally re-certified.
Historical corrected source-aware v2 failure is preserved; this lexical experiment adds no paid-run recommendation.
